exposure: pandemic-related changes to maternity care practices
outcome: not feeling safe giving birth in the hospital
cohort: The study included 885 women who gave birth in US hospitals between March and July 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic.
finding: Many women reported inadequate support (61%) and not feeling safe (20.5%) while giving birth during the pandemic, and those who tested positive for COVID-19 were more likely to experience cesarean delivery, lack a birth partner, and discontinue breastfeeding early.
mod_finding: Women who tested positive for COVID-19 were more likely to have a cesarean delivery.
cross-section timing: Women who gave birth between March and July 2020.
